title: Phacoemulsification with IOL implantation combined with goniosynechialysis and goniotomy in primary angle-closure glaucoma following failed trabeculectomy: short-term effectiveness and safety outcomes

indication: moderate to advanced primary angle-closure glaucoma with PAS > 180 degrees and visually significant cataract, medically uncontrolled on maximal tolerated therapy, age >= 40 years; subgroups by surgical history: surgically naive eyes and eyes after failed trabeculectomy (flat/encapsulated non-functioning bleb); retrospective comparative case series (Nanjing, China)

groups.description: surgically naive PACG eyes undergoing phacoemulsification with IOL implantation, goniosynechialysis and about 120-degree goniotomy with the LAN microhook (PEI-GSL-GT); n from Table 1/2 headers (T2!R1C2)
PACG eyes after at least one failed trabeculectomy undergoing the same PEI-GSL-GT procedure; n from Table 1/2 headers (T2!R1C3)

series.baseline_label: Table 2 'Preoperative' block, row 'IOP (mmHg)' (same mean as Table 1 'Baseline IOP (mmHg)', T1!R4C2)
series.notes: IOP cells are mean ± SD (the footnote allows mean ± SD or median (IQR); IOP rows are formatted 'mean ± SD' and the Results quote them as mean IOP); blocks Preoperative, 1 Day, 1 week, 1 month, 3 months postop; n = 22 in the header for all time points; eyes lost to follow-up before 3 months were excluded from the cohort (ordinary attrition)

series.baseline_label: Table 2 'Preoperative' block, row 'IOP (mmHg)' (Table 1 'Baseline IOP (mmHg)', T1!R4C3, gives the same mean with one more SD decimal)
series.notes: IOP cells are mean ± SD; blocks Preoperative, 1 Day, 1 week, 1 month, 3 months postop; n = 17 in the header for all time points; two eyes had day-1 IOP spikes treated by anterior chamber paracentesis (standard postoperative care)

exclusions.what: Table 2 'Absolute reduction of IOP (mmHg)' and 'Percentage reduction of IOP (%)' rows (R19, R20)
exclusions.reason: the same table gives absolute IOP; absolute series used (brief rule)

exclusions.what: Table 2 P-value columns and rows (C4, R21, R22)

exclusions.reason: medians and medication numbers are not admissible IOP series; noted only

exclusions.what: qualified/complete success counts and Kaplan-Meier analysis (Figure 5)
exclusions.reason: success proportions / Kaplan-Meier estimates are not admissible

exclusions.what: Figure 3 waterfall plots of per-eye percentage IOP reduction
exclusions.reason: figure-only percentage changes, not cited table cells

notes: Reference kind 'preoperative_medicated': inclusion required medically uncontrolled IOP despite maximal tolerated medical therapy; preoperative medication numbers are tabulated (T2!R4C2, T2!R4C3, medians); no washout described.
Tonometer: non-contact tonometer, average of three consecutive readings by the same ophthalmologist, preoperatively and at every follow-up (method 'noncontact').
Day 1 and Week 1 converted as 1/30.4375 and 7/30.4375 months (rounded to 4 decimals).

Both groups received the same standard combined procedure; the groups are defined by preoperative surgical history, so both are 'control' groups. Both eyes of some patients are included (39 eyes of 33 patients).

Postoperative transient IOP elevation was managed by resuming anti-glaucoma medications or anterior chamber paracentesis (standard care); no outcome-defined exclusion of eyes from the Table 2 means is stated.
